newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates fluctuate.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates fluctuate.

text.p: Dutch call money rates fluctuated between 2.50 and just above 3.00 percent bid on Wednesday as some participants tried to fill a liquidity gap only two days ahead of the cash reserve expiry, dealers said.
Dealers said business was not hectic, but they noted some demand for call money because liquidity had not been evenly divided among money market players.
"Some business was done at 3.125 percent bid," said one dealer, adding it was only in small amounts.
"Some participants have to fill a small gap ahead of the cash reserve expiry," said another dealer.
He expected call money to remain near 2.75 percent bid until Friday and it would probably rise close to 3.00 percent when the new cash reserve arrangement starts running.
Call money rates usually linger near the rate for the special advances, currently 2.90 percent.
The Dutch central bank will set a new advances pact, which runs for up to a week, on Thursday afternoon.
Other money rates were stable, with three-month deposits bid at an unchanged 3.12 percent bid.
The guilder was little changed at 112.5275 per 100 marks from 112.515 on Tuesday.
